personality_one_liner: A clinical, trustworthy, and calm medical utility that prioritizes clarity, progressive disclosure, and precision.

spacing.rule: Maintain strict, generous vertical rhythm. Use `md` (12) for internal padding of cards, and `xl` (24) to separate major sections. The interface must feel breathable and uncrowded.

do's: Use on the bottom tab bar.
Use on the sticky CTA container at the bottom of the Results screen to maintain context while scrolling.
Use for the trial countdown banner if floating over content.
dont's: Never use glass on medical result cards or critical data - clarity beats aesthetics here.
Never use behind body text or form inputs.

screens.name: Auth (Login/Signup)
screens.layout: Hero image at the top with a vertical gradient scrim fading into `surface`. Clean, clinical input fields (labels above inputs). Primary CTA sticky to the keyboard.

states.error: Standard inline validation and toasts for auth failures.

screens.name: Home / History (Tab 1)
screens.purpose: Dashboard showing trial status and previous scans.
screens.layout: Top banner displays '7-Day Free Trial' with a live minute-by-minute countdown. Below: A list of past analysis cards. Each card shows a small thumbnail, date, and top diagnosis. A large, prominent FAB (Floating Action Button) centered above the tab bar for 'New Scan'.

states.empty: Branded illustration or soft texture with text: 'No scans yet. Tap the + button to capture your first skin lesion.'
states.error: Text: 'Unable to load history.' with Retry button.

screens.name: About (Tab 2)
screens.purpose: Information about the app, version, and general medical disclaimers.
screens.layout: Standard list view with sections: App Version, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and a prominent 'Not Medical Advice' card.

screens.name: Capture Modal
screens.purpose: Camera interface to capture or upload skin lesion.
screens.layout: Full-screen camera view (dark UI). A clear rectangular guide frame/viewfinder in the center with corner brackets to indicate the scanning zone. 'Align lesion within the frame' instructional text below it. Large capture ring at the bottom, with a gallery upload icon on the side.

states.loading: Processing overlay with 'Analyzing Image...' text and spinner.
states.error: Camera permission denied message with CTA to open settings.

screens.name: Analysis Result
screens.purpose: Display AI findings clearly and clinically.
screens.layout: Scrollable view. Top: Image thumbnail with a 'Quality Assessment' pill (e.g., 'Quality: Excellent' in green). Below: 'Most Likely Diagnosis' modular card featuring Disease Name, Confidence % (in Mono font), Urgency Badge (Traffic light color-coded: Green/Yellow/Red), and Description. Next: 'Differential Diagnoses' accordion cards. Next: 'Recommended Next Steps' list. Bottom: A prominent Medical Disclaimer card with a warning icon. Sticky footer CTA: 'Share / Download PDF'.

screens.name: Device Activation
screens.purpose: Post-trial lock screen for offline activation.
screens.layout: Full-screen lockdown modal (no close button). Headline: 'Activate this Device'. Shows the hardware 'Device ID' in a Mono font card with a 'Copy' icon. Below: GCash QR Code image centered. Below QR: Text input for 'Activation Key'. Large 'Activate' primary CTA.

instructions_to_main_agent: Use the Sage Green palette defined in the JSON. Never use Indigo, Violet, or Blue. Strict adherence to WCAG AA contrast.

Implement the layout with Plus Jakarta Sans for titles/display, Geist for body text, and Space Grotesk specifically for numeric data (Confidence %, Trial Countdown, Device ID) to reinforce the clinical, precise feel.
For the Results screen, use a 'Traffic Light' semantic color system (success/warning/error tokens) to represent the Urgency Badge of the diagnosis, reducing cognitive load.
The 7-day free trial countdown must be prominently displayed as a live timer (down to the minute) in a floating or sticky banner on the Home tab.
On the Device Activation screen, present a mock GCash QR code (you can use a placeholder SVG/QR library) and display the Device ID in a copyable card.
Generate a PDF using `expo-print` or `expo-sharing` containing the diagnosis data when the user taps 'Share / Download PDF' on the Results screen.
For the History empty state, if you cannot find a suitable illustration, use a large, tinted Phosphor/Ionicons icon encapsulated in a `brandTertiary` rounded square.
Ensure the Capture Screen uses a dark theme regardless of system setting for better viewfinder contrast, placing a rectangular guide frame overlay on the camera view.
